masthead.headline: The console's own palette, type and components, shown rather than described.
masthead.lede: Everything below is drawn with the tokens it documents, so a value that has drifted shows up as a drawing that looks wrong rather than as a table that reads right.

sections.label: The surface
sections.title: What the console actually looks like in use.

blocks.text: Meridian is read standing up, on a wall-mounted screen, by someone holding a scanner. That is the whole justification for the density below: a row is 72 pixels tall because a glove-width tap target is, not because the grid said so.

blocks.title: Orders console, default view
blocks.alt: The orders console: a dark left rail, a filter row, and a table of seven orders each ending in a coloured status pill.
blocks.caption: Captured at 800 by 500. The three status colours are the only hues in the interface that are not the accent.

pins.text: The rail is the one dark surface. It never holds content the reader has to read closely — only where they are.
Filters are chips, not a dropdown: the current filter has to be visible from three metres away.

text: Status is a filled pill, and the word inside it is the status. Colour is the

blocks.title: Order row: resting and focused
blocks.alt: An order row at 72 pixels tall with an accent bar, an order number, a status pill and an open button; below it the same row with a three-pixel focus ring drawn four pixels outside its border.

pins.text: The accent bar is 4 pixels and load-bearing: it is what distinguishes an order that needs attention from one that does not, at a distance where the pill is unreadable.
The focus ring sits outside the row rather than inside it, so focus never changes the row's own geometry and nothing shifts as the reader tabs.

blocks.summary: Why the accent is stated as a hue rather than as a hex value

blocks.text: A board declares one number — the accent hue — and the light and dark ramps are derived from it at the lightness and chroma the built-in tokens already use. Two hex values would have to be chosen, checked for contrast, and then kept in step by hand forever.
